sections.title: Step 1: Text Cleaning
sections.body:
```python
class TextPreprocessor:
    """Complete text preprocessing pipeline"""
    
    def __init__(self):
        # Download required NLTK data
        try:
            self.stop_words = set(stopwords.words('english'))
            self.stemmer = PorterStemmer()
            self.lemmatizer = WordNetLemmatizer()
        except:
            nltk.download('stopwords')
            nltk.download('punkt')
            nltk.download('wordnet')
            nltk.download('averaged_perceptron_tagger')
            self.stop_words = set(stopwords.words('english'))
            self.stemmer = PorterStemmer()
            self.lemmatizer = WordNetLemmatizer()
    
    def clean_text(self, text):
        """
        Clean text: lowercase, remove special chars, extra spaces
        """
        # Convert to lowercase
        text = text.lower()
        
        # Remove URLs
        text = re.sub(r'http\S+|www\S+|https\S+', '', text)
        
        # Remove email addresses
        text = re.sub(r'\S+@\S+', '', text)
        
        # Remove HTML tags
        text = re.sub(r'<.*?>', '', text)
        
        # Remove numbers (optional - depends on use case)
        # text = re.sub(r'\d+', '', text)
        
        # Remove special characters and punctuation
        text = re.sub(r'[^a-zA-Z0-9\s]', '', text)
        
        # Remove extra whitespaces
        text = re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', text).strip()
        
        return text
    
    def tokenize(self, text):
        """Split text into words (tokens)"""
        return word_tokenize(text)
    
    def remove_stopwords(self, tokens):
        """Remove common words (the, is, at, which, on...)"""
        return [word for word in tokens if word not in self.stop_words]
    
    def stem_tokens(self, tokens):
        """
        Stemming: Reduce words to root form (crude)
        running → run, flies → fli, studies → studi
        """
        return [self.stemmer.stem(word) for word in tokens]
    
    def lemmatize_tokens(self, tokens):
        """
        Lemmatization: Reduce words to base form (proper)
        running → run, flies → fly, studies → study
        """
        return [self.lemmatizer.lemmatize(word) for word in tokens]
    
    def preprocess(self, text, remove_stops=True, use_lemma=True):
        """Complete preprocessing pipeline"""
        # Clean text
        text = self.clean_text(text)
        
        # Tokenize
        tokens = self.tokenize(text)
        
        # Remove stopwords
        if remove_stops:
            tokens = self.remove_stopwords(tokens)
        
        # Lemmatize or stem
        if use_lemma:
            tokens = self.lemmatize_tokens(tokens)
        else:
            tokens = self.stem_tokens(tokens)
        
        return tokens

# Example usage
preprocessor = TextPreprocessor()

sample_text = """
Natural Language Processing (NLP) is a fascinating field! 
It allows computers to understand, interpret, and generate human language.
Visit https://example.com for more info. Contact us at info@example.com
"""

print("\nOriginal Text:")
print(sample_text)

print("\nCleaned Text:")
cleaned = preprocessor.clean_text(sample_text)
print(cleaned)

print("\nTokenized:")
tokens = preprocessor.tokenize(cleaned)
print(tokens)

print("\nAfter Removing Stopwords:")
no_stops = preprocessor.remove_stopwords(tokens)
print(no_stops)

print("\nAfter Stemming:")
stemmed = preprocessor.stem_tokens(no_stops)
print(stemmed)

print("\nAfter Lemmatization:")
lemmatized = preprocessor.lemmatize_tokens(no_stops)
print(lemmatized)

print("\nComplete Preprocessing:")
final = preprocessor.preprocess(sample_text)
print(final)
```

**Tokenization Techniques:**

1. Word Tokenization (Split by spaces/punctuation):
"Hello, world!" → ["Hello", ",", "world", "!"]

2. Sentence Tokenization:
"Hello. How are you?" → ["Hello.", "How are you?"]

3. Subword Tokenization (for transformers - covered in Topic 180):
"unhappiness" → ["un", "happiness"]

4. Character Tokenization:
"cat" → ["c", "a", "t"]

```python
# Sentence tokenization example
text = "Natural language processing is amazing. It enables many applications. Try it yourself!"
sentences = sent_tokenize(text)
print("\nSentence Tokenization Example:")
for i, sent in enumerate(sentences, 1):
    print(f"Sentence {i}: {sent}")
```

**STEMMING vs LEMMATIZATION:**

**Stemming (Crude, Fast):**
- caring → car
- organization → organ
- generously → generous
- studies → studi

**Lemmatization (Accurate, Slower):**
- caring → care
- organization → organization
- generously → generously
- studies → study

**When to use:**
✅ Stemming: Fast processing, search engines, large corpus
✅ Lemmatization: Accuracy matters, small corpus, final output

🎒 TOPIC 164B: BAG OF WORDS (BOW) & TF-IDF

Bag of Words: Represent text as word frequency vectors
- Ignores word order
- Simple and effective
- Baseline for text classification

TF-IDF: Weighted Bag of Words
- TF = Term Frequency
- IDF = Inverse Document Frequency
- Highlights important words

```python
# BAG OF WORDS (BOW)
print("BAG OF WORDS (BOW)")

corpus = [
    "I love machine learning",
    "I love deep learning",
    "Deep learning is amazing",
    "Machine learning is powerful"
]

print("\nCorpus:")
for i, doc in enumerate(corpus, 1):
    print(f"{i}. {doc}")

# Create Bag of Words
vectorizer = CountVectorizer()
bow_matrix = vectorizer.fit_transform(corpus)

# Get vocabulary
vocab = vectorizer.get_feature_names_out()
print(f"\nVocabulary ({len(vocab)} words):")
print(vocab)

# Show BOW matrix
bow_df = pd.DataFrame(
    bow_matrix.toarray(),
    columns=vocab,
    index=[f"Doc {i}" for i in range(1, len(corpus)+1)]
)

print("\nBag of Words Matrix:")
print(bow_df)
```

**Explanation:**
- Each row = one document
- Each column = one word from vocabulary
- Values = word counts

Example: "I love machine learning"
- {'i': 1, 'love': 1, 'machine': 1, 'learning': 1}

**Limitations:**
❌ No word order: "dog bites man" = "man bites dog"
❌ No semantics: "good" and "excellent" are different
❌ Common words dominate (the, is, a)
❌ High dimensionality (|vocabulary| can be huge)

```python
# TF-IDF
print("TF-IDF (Term Frequency - Inverse Document Frequency)")
```

**Formula:**
TF-IDF(word, doc) = TF(word, doc) × IDF(word)

```python
TF(word, doc) = (# of times word appears in doc) / (# of words in doc)
IDF(word) = log(Total documents / Documents containing word)
```

**Intuition:**
✅ High TF-IDF → Word is important IN THIS document
✅ Low TF-IDF → Word is common across all documents

**Example:**
- "the" appears in all docs → Low IDF → Low TF-IDF
- "quantum" appears in 1 doc → High IDF → High TF-IDF

```python
# Create TF-IDF
tfidf_vectorizer = TfidfVectorizer()
tfidf_matrix = tfidf_vectorizer.fit_transform(corpus)

tfidf_df = pd.DataFrame(
    tfidf_matrix.toarray(),
    columns=tfidf_vectorizer.get_feature_names_out(),
    index=[f"Doc {i}" for i in range(1, len(corpus)+1)]
)

print("\nTF-IDF Matrix:")
print(tfidf_df.round(3))
```

**Notice:**
- Common words ("is", "learning") have lower values
- Unique words have higher values
- Better for finding important/distinctive words

```python
# Text Classification with BOW and TF-IDF
print("TEXT CLASSIFICATION EXAMPLE")

# Sample dataset: Movie reviews
train_texts = [
    "This movie was amazing and fantastic",
    "Great film with excellent acting",
    "Wonderful storyline and great characters",
    "Terrible movie with bad acting",
    "Awful film, waste of time",
    "Boring and poorly made"
]

train_labels = [1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0]  # 1 = positive, 0 = negative

test_texts = [
    "Amazing film with great story",
    "Bad movie, terrible acting"
]

print("\nTraining Data:")
for text, label in zip(train_texts, train_labels):
    sentiment = "Positive" if label == 1 else "Negative"
    print(f"[{sentiment}] {text}")

# Method 1: BOW + Naive Bayes
print("\n--- Method 1: Bag of Words + Naive Bayes ---")
bow_vec = CountVectorizer()
X_train_bow = bow_vec.fit_transform(train_texts)
X_test_bow = bow_vec.transform(test_texts)

clf_bow = MultinomialNB()
clf_bow.fit(X_train_bow, train_labels)

predictions_bow = clf_bow.predict(X_test_bow)
probabilities_bow = clf_bow.predict_proba(X_test_bow)

print("\nTest Results (BOW):")
for text, pred, proba in zip(test_texts, predictions_bow, probabilities_bow):
    sentiment = "Positive" if pred == 1 else "Negative"
    confidence = proba[pred]
    print(f"{text}")
    print(f"  → {sentiment} (confidence: {confidence:.2%})")

# Method 2: TF-IDF + Logistic Regression
print("\n--- Method 2: TF-IDF + Logistic Regression ---")
tfidf_vec = TfidfVectorizer()
X_train_tfidf = tfidf_vec.fit_transform(train_texts)
X_test_tfidf = tfidf_vec.transform(test_texts)

clf_tfidf = LogisticRegression()
clf_tfidf.fit(X_train_tfidf, train_labels)

predictions_tfidf = clf_tfidf.predict(X_test_tfidf)
probabilities_tfidf = clf_tfidf.predict_proba(X_test_tfidf)

print("\nTest Results (TF-IDF):")
for text, pred, proba in zip(test_texts, predictions_tfidf, probabilities_tfidf):
    sentiment = "Positive" if pred == 1 else "Negative"
    confidence = proba[pred]
    print(f"{text}")
    print(f"  → {sentiment} (confidence: {confidence:.2%})")

# Show most important features
print("\nMost Important Words (TF-IDF):")
feature_names = tfidf_vec.get_feature_names_out()
coefficients = clf_tfidf.coef_[0]

# Top positive words
top_positive_idx = coefficients.argsort()[-5:][::-1]
print("\nPositive words:")
for idx in top_positive_idx:
    print(f"  {feature_names[idx]}: {coefficients[idx]:.3f}")

# Top negative words
top_negative_idx = coefficients.argsort()[:5]
print("\nNegative words:")
for idx in top_negative_idx:
    print(f"  {feature_names[idx]}: {coefficients[idx]:.3f}")
```

**Bow & Tf-Idf Variants:**

1. Binary BOW:
```python
vectorizer = CountVectorizer(binary=True)
# 1 if word present, 0 if absent (ignore frequency)
```

2. N-grams:
```python
vectorizer = CountVectorizer(ngram_range=(1, 2))
# Capture word pairs: "not good" vs "good"
```

3. Min/Max Document Frequency:
```python
vectorizer = TfidfVectorizer(min_df=2, max_df=0.8)
# min_df: Ignore rare words
# max_df: Ignore too common words
```

4. Sublinear TF:
```python
vectorizer = TfidfVectorizer(sublinear_tf=True)
# TF = 1 + log(TF) - reduces impact of high frequency
```

**When to Use:**
✅ BOW: Simple baseline, document classification
✅ TF-IDF: Information retrieval, keyword extraction
✅ N-grams: Sentiment analysis (capture negation)
✅ Baseline before trying deep learning!

🔢 TOPIC 164C: WORD EMBEDDINGS (Word2Vec, GloVe, FastText)

Word Embeddings: Dense vector representations of words
- Capture semantic meaning
- Similar words → Similar vectors
- Enable arithmetic: king - man + woman ≈ queen

**Evolution:**
One-Hot Encoding → BOW/TF-IDF → Word Embeddings → Contextual Embeddings (BERT)

```python
# Word2Vec Concepts
print("WORD2VEC")
```

**Two Architectures:**

1. CBOW (Continuous Bag of Words):
Input: Context words → Output: Target word
Example: "The cat ___ on the mat" → "sat"

2. Skip-gram:
Input: Target word → Output: Context words
Example: "sat" → ["the", "cat", "on", "the", "mat"]

Skip-gram is better for rare words!

**Training:**
- Sliding window over text
- Predict context from word (or vice versa)
- Backprop updates embeddings
- Negative sampling for efficiency

```python
# Word2Vec Implementation (using gensim)
print("\nWord2Vec Implementation:")

try:
    from gensim.models import Word2Vec
    from gensim.models.phrases import Phrases, Phraser
    
    # Sample corpus
    sentences = [
        ['machine', 'learning', 'is', 'fun'],
        ['deep', 'learning', 'is', 'powerful'],
        ['machine', 'learning', 'models', 'learn', 'patterns'],
        ['deep', 'neural', 'networks', 'are', 'powerful'],
        ['natural', 'language', 'processing', 'is', 'interesting'],
        ['nlp', 'uses', 'machine', 'learning'],
        ['transformers', 'revolutionized', 'nlp'],
        ['bert', 'is', 'a', 'transformer', 'model']
    ]
    
    print("\nTraining Word2Vec model...")
    
    # Train Word2Vec
    model = Word2Vec(
        sentences=sentences,
        vector_size=50,        # Embedding dimension
        window=3,              # Context window size
        min_count=1,           # Minimum word frequency
        sg=1,                  # 1=Skip-gram, 0=CBOW
        epochs=100,
        seed=42
    )
    
    print(f"Vocabulary size: {len(model.wv)}")
    print(f"Vector dimension: {model.wv.vector_size}")
    
    # Get word vector
    word = 'machine'
    if word in model.wv:
        vector = model.wv[word]
        print(f"\nVector for '{word}' (first 10 dims):")
        print(vector[:10])
    
    # Find similar words
    print(f"\nWords most similar to 'machine':")
    similar = model.wv.most_similar('machine', topn=3)
    for word, score in similar:
        print(f"  {word}: {score:.3f}")
    
    # Word arithmetic
    try:
        result = model.wv.most_similar(
            positive=['deep', 'learning'],
            negative=['machine'],
            topn=3
        )
        print(f"\ndeep + learning - machine =")
        for word, score in result:
            print(f"  {word}: {score:.3f}")
    except:
        print("\nWord arithmetic requires more training data")
    
    # Compute similarity
    sim = model.wv.similarity('deep', 'machine')
    print(f"\nSimilarity(deep, machine): {sim:.3f}")
    
except ImportError:
    print("\nInstall gensim: pip install gensim")
```

```python
# GloVe
print("GloVe (Global Vectors)")
```

**GloVe combines:**
- Global matrix factorization (LSA)
- Local context window (Word2Vec)

**Key Idea:**
- Build co-occurrence matrix (how often words appear together)
- Factorize matrix to get embeddings
- Preserves word relationships

**Formula:**
w_i^T * w_j + b_i + b_j = log(X_ij)
where X_ij = # times word i and j co-occur

**Pre-trained GloVe:**
- Wikipedia 2014 + Gigaword 5 (6B tokens)
- Common Crawl (42B/840B tokens)
- Dimensions: 50, 100, 200, 300

**Usage:**
```python
# Download from: https://nlp.stanford.edu/projects/glove/
```

```python
import numpy as np
```

```python
def load_glove(file_path):
    embeddings = {}
    with open(file_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        for line in f:
            values = line.split()
            word = values[0]
            vector = np.array(values[1:], dtype='float32')
            embeddings[word] = vector
    return embeddings
```

**FastText (by Facebook):**
- Extension of Word2Vec
- Represents words as BAG OF CHARACTER N-GRAMS
- Better for rare/unknown words

**Example:**
Word: "unhappiness"
N-grams (n=3): <un, unh, nha, hap, app, ppi, pin, ine, nes, ss>

```python
Embedding = Average of n-gram embeddings
```

**Advantages:**
✅ Handle out-of-vocabulary words
✅ Better for morphologically rich languages
✅ Good for rare words
✅ Capture sub-word information

Example: Even if "unhappiness" not in vocab,
can infer from: "un" (negative) + "happy" + "ness" (noun)

**When To Use What:**

1. BOW/TF-IDF:
✅ Quick baseline
✅ Small datasets
✅ Interpretable features
✅ Simple classification
❌ No semantic understanding

2. Word2Vec/GloVe:
✅ Transfer learning (use pre-trained)
✅ Semantic similarity
✅ Document clustering
✅ Feature extraction for ML
❌ OOV words are problem

3. FastText:
✅ Languages with rich morphology
✅ Many rare/unknown words
✅ Character-level understanding
❌ Slightly slower than Word2Vec

4. Modern: Contextual Embeddings (BERT - Topic 164):
✅ Context-dependent meanings
✅ State-of-the-art performance
✅ Transfer learning
❌ Computationally expensive

**Evolution:**
One-Hot (1990s) → BOW/TF-IDF (2000s) → Word2Vec (2013) →
GloVe (2014) → FastText (2016) → ELMo (2018) → BERT (2018) →
GPT/T5 (2019+) → Modern LLMs (2020+)

**Practical Tips:**

1. Start Simple:
- Always try BOW/TF-IDF first
- Set baseline performance
- Then try advanced methods

2. Data Preprocessing:
- Clean text thoroughly
- Remove stopwords (or not - depends on task)
- Lemmatize > Stem (usually)

3. Feature Engineering:
- Try different n-gram ranges
- Combine BOW + other features
- Use TF-IDF for importance

4. Embeddings:
- Use pre-trained when possible
- Fine-tune on domain data
- Average/pool embeddings for sentences

5. Evaluation:
- Cross-validation
- Test on unseen data
- Compare multiple approaches

sections.title: Topic 164: BERT Deep Dive
sections.body:
**Architecture Review:**
- Bidirectional Transformer Encoder
- 12 layers (base), 24 layers (large)
- Pre-training: MLM + NSP
- Fine-tuning for downstream tasks

**Pre-training Objectives:**
1. Masked Language Modeling (MLM):
Input:  "The [MASK] sat on the mat"
Target: "cat"
- Mask 15% of tokens
- Predict masked tokens
- Bidirectional context!

2. Next Sentence Prediction (NSP):
Input:  [CLS] Sent A [SEP] Sent B [SEP]
Label:  IsNext (1) or NotNext (0)
- Learn sentence relationships

**Fine-tuning Strategies:**
✅ Full fine-tuning: Update all parameters
✅ Feature extraction: Freeze BERT, train classifier
✅ Layer-wise LR decay: Lower LR for lower layers
✅ Gradual unfreezing: Unfreeze layers progressively

**Usage:**

sections.title: Topic 166: ALBERT (A Lite BERT)
sections.body:
Key Innovation: Parameter Reduction
- Factorized embedding: E ≪ H
- Cross-layer parameter sharing
- 18× fewer parameters than BERT-large!

**Changes:**
✅ Sentence Order Prediction (SOP) instead of NSP
✅ Shared weights across layers
✅ Factorized embeddings

**Trade-offs:**
- Fewer parameters ✅
- Slower inference (shared weights) ❌
- Similar performance ✅

sections.title: Topic 167: DistilBERT (Distilled BERT)
sections.body:
**Knowledge Distillation:**
- Student learns from Teacher (BERT)
- 40% smaller, 60% faster
- Retains 97% of performance!

**Loss Function:**
```python
L = α·L_ce + (1-α)·L_distill + β·L_cos
```

where:
- L_ce: Cross-entropy with true labels
- L_distill: KL divergence with teacher
- L_cos: Cosine similarity of hidden states

**Use Cases:**
✅ Mobile applications
✅ Edge devices
✅ Real-time inference

sections.title: Topic 172: Decoding Strategies
sections.body:
1. Greedy Decoding:
```python
token = argmax(P(w_t | context))
```
- Fast
- Deterministic
- Repetitive

2. Beam Search:
- Keep top-k sequences
- More diverse than greedy
- Still somewhat repetitive

3. Top-k Sampling:
- Sample from top k tokens
- More random
- Better diversity

4. Top-p (Nucleus) Sampling:
- Sample from smallest set with cumulative prob ≥ p
- Dynamic vocabulary size
- Best for generation!

5. Temperature Scaling:
P'(w) = P(w)^(1/T) / Σ P(w_i)^(1/T)

- T < 1: More confident (peaked)
- T > 1: More random (flat)
- T = 0.7-0.9: Good balance

sections.title: Topic 177: FINE-TUNING LLMS (LoRA, QLoRA)
sections.body:
Challenge: LLMs are huge (7B-70B+ parameters)
Solution: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT)

**LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation):**
- Add trainable low-rank matrices
- Freeze pre-trained weights
- W' = W + ΔW = W + BA
- Only train A, B (much smaller!)

Reduction: 10,000× fewer parameters!

**Implementation:**
from peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body:
lora_config = LoraConfig(
```python
 r=8,  # rank
 lora_alpha=32,
 target_modules=["q_proj", "v_proj"],
 lora_dropout=0.05,
 bias="none",
 task_type="CAUSAL_LM"
```
)

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body:
model = get_peft_model(model, lora_config)
model.print_trainable_parameters()

**QLoRA (Quantized LoRA):**
- 4-bit quantization + LoRA
- Train 65B model on single 48GB GPU!
- Minimal quality loss

bnb_config = BitsAndBytesConfig(
```python
 load_in_4bit=True,
 bnb_4bit_quant_type="nf4",
 bnb_4bit_compute_dtype=torch.float16
```
)

model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
"meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf",
```python
 quantization_config=bnb_config
```
)

**Benefits:**
✅ 10-1000× fewer parameters to train
✅ Faster training
✅ Less memory
✅ Modular (swap LoRA adapters)

sections.title: Topic 180: Tokenization Deep Dive
sections.body:
**Subword Tokenization:**

1. Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE):
- Start with characters
- Merge most frequent pairs
- GPT-2, GPT-3 use BPE

2. WordPiece:
- Similar to BPE
- Likelihood-based merging
- BERT uses WordPiece

3. SentencePiece:
- Language-agnostic
- Trains directly on raw text
- T5, ALBERT use SentencePiece

4. Unigram:
- Start with large vocabulary
- Prune based on likelihood

**Trade-offs:**
- Vocabulary size vs granularity
- Common words = single token
- Rare words = multiple tokens

from transformers import AutoTokenizer

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("gpt2")
tokens = tokenizer.tokenize("Hello world!")
ids = tokenizer.encode("Hello world!")
text = tokenizer.decode(ids)

sections.title: Topic 181: Context Length Handling
sections.body:
Problem: Transformers have fixed context (512, 2048, 4096)

**Solutions:**

1. Truncation:
- Keep first/last N tokens
- Simple but loses information

2. Chunking + Summarization:
- Split into chunks
- Summarize each
- Combine summaries

3. Hierarchical Attention:
- Local attention + global attention
- Longformer, BigBird

4. Position Interpolation:
- Interpolate positional embeddings
- Extend context cheaply

5. Sliding Window:
- Process overlapping windows
- Combine results

6. Retrieval:
- Don't process everything
- Retrieve relevant chunks (RAG)
